newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GMA expects A$30-35 mln writedown.
newsitem.headline: GMA expects A$30-35 mln writedown.

text.p: Gold Mines of Australia Ltd said on Wednesday it expected to include a write-down of between A$30 million and A$35 million in the book value of gold development and exploration costs in its accounts for the year to June 30.

GMA also said it had agreed to sell its Youanmi gold mine in Western Australia to Kirkwood Gold NL for A$8 million and that it expected gold production in 1997/98 of about 40,000 ounces to 45,000 ounces.
Kirkwood Gold is the parent company of Scomac Mining, the contractor at Youanmi.
Kirkwood is a subsidiary of Rhodes Mining N.L..
GMA said the sale was part of GMA's previously announced strategy of concentrating on its Mt Lyell copper mine in Tasmania and the Reedy gold mine in Western Australia.
GMA said it planned operational changes at Reedy designed to optimise profitability while further exploring the NOA deposit which it said was promising.
"Production in 1997/98 will be focused on sources of ore which can generate satisfactory returns at the current gold price," GMA said.

"We are confident that the exploration program will significantly increase the economic reserves leading to reinstatement of larger scale operations in due course," GMA Chairman Andrew Love said in a statement.
GMA said the write-downs would have little impact on future cash flows as they were mostly non-cash accounting write-offs.
"Future earnings will reflect the benefit of lower depreciation and amortisation charges," the company said.
GMA's shares closed down half a cent on Tuesday at 10 cents.
